items.title: What Happens to Mortgage Rates Post Midterms?

items.title: Goldman Sachs Sees Mortgage Rates Falling to 6.4% in 2027
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Goldman Sachs just put out their 2027 housing outlook and the good news is it has mortgage rates coming down next year. And by a healthy margin at that, with the popular 30-year fixed sliding to 6.4% at some point. That’s nearly a full percentage point below current levels, which have hovered around 7.25% to… Read More »

items.title: Tech Selloff Keeps Pushing Mortgage Rates Closer to the 6s
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Mortgage rates are even lower today, inching their way closer and closer to a 6-handle. And once again tech stocks are getting hammered, pushing a lot of money toward the safety of bonds. When that happens, their corresponding yields (or interest rates) drop, and that spells relief for mortgage rates. The bellwether 10-year bond yield… Read More »

items.title: Zillow’s New Zero-Down FHA Loan Comes at an Interesting Time
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Zillow’s lending department, known as Zillow Home Loans, or ZHL for short, just rolled out a way for eligible home buyers to get an FHA loan with no money down. items.title: Mortgage Rates Catch a Small Break Despite Hot GDP
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Mortgage rates are a hair better today, with bond yields moving back below 5% on cooler-than-expected inflation. At last glance, the bellwether 10-year bond yield was down about six basis points to around 4.98%. That’s thanks to a mixed bag of economic reports released this morning, including PCE and GDP. items.title: AI Spending Hot Again, Remains the Wild Card for Mortgage Rates
